newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says European unity is more than money.
newsitem.headline: Italy says European unity is more than money.

text.p: Italy said on Thursday the unification of Europe must be built upon "fundamental" issues like civil rights and employment and not just on economic and monetary union.
Foreign Minister Lamberto Dini's office said in a statement that the government had discussed Italy's strategies regarding the EU in a cabinet meeting on Thursday.

The statement said that, besides working to meet tough criteria for economic and monetary union, Italy would also seek to promote other key issues related to European unity such as civil rights and employment.
"Italy intends to act so that other fundmental dimensions of European unity are developed," the statement said.
It listed civil rights, social issues, employment, justice, internal affairs, security and foreign policy as key topics.

The statement said that Europe had a golden opportunity to broaden the 15-nation bloc's goals for unity when EU foreign ministers meet in Rome on March 25 to discuss progress on the reform of EU institutions.
The meeting will also celebrate the 40th anniversary of the Treaty of Rome, which established the European Community.
